title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #534: Maximum GCD-Intersecting Sets**

What is the largest $A \subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ containing $N$ with $\gcd(a,b) > 1$ for all distinct $a,b \in A$? This is an arithmetic version of Erdős-Ko-Rado intersecting family problems, where $\gcd > 1$ replaces 'shares a set element'. The original Erdős-Graham conjecture was WRONG — Ahlswede and Khachatrian found a counterexample (1992) and proved the correct characterization (1996) using optimal families based on the prime factorization of $N$.
mathContext: Maximize |A| subject to A ⊆ {1,...,N}, N ∈ A, and ∀ a b ∈ A, a ≠ b → Nat.gcd a b > 1

title: Core Definitions
content: **interval N**: The set $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ constructed via `Finset.range N` with a `+1` shift embedding, avoiding zero. **IsGCDIntersecting A**: For all distinct $a,b \in A$, $\gcd(a,b) > 1$ — every pair shares a common prime factor. This is the arithmetic analog of the 'intersecting' property in classical extremal set theory. **ContainsN A N**: The constraint $N \in A$, ensuring the target number is included. **maxGCDIntersecting N**: The supremum of achievable cardinalities of GCD-intersecting subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ containing $N$, defined via `sSup`.

title: Simple Constructions
content: **multiplesOfSmallestPrime N**: All multiples of $p = \text{minFac}(N)$ in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, giving a set of size $\lfloor N/p \rfloor$. Since every element is divisible by $p$, all pairs share the common factor $p$, making this GCD-intersecting. **evenMultiplesSharing N**: Even numbers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ that also share a factor with $N$. All pairs have $\gcd \geq 2$ since both are even. These two constructions represent the candidates from the original (incorrect) Erdős-Graham conjecture: the maximum was conjectured to be $\max(N/p, |\text{evenMultiplesSharing}(N)|)$.
mathContext:
multiplesOfSmallestPrime N = (interval N).filter (fun n => N.minFac ∣ n)
evenMultiplesSharing N = (interval N).filter (fun n => 2 ∣ n ∧ Nat.gcd n N > 1)
multiples_of_p_size: card = N / N.minFac
multiples_of_p_intersecting: IsGCDIntersecting (multiplesOfSmallestPrime N)

title: Original Conjecture (WRONG)
content: **OriginalConjecture**: Erdős and Graham conjectured that the maximum GCD-intersecting set size equals $\max(\lfloor N/p \rfloor, |\text{evenMultiplesSharing}(N)|)$, where $p$ is the smallest prime factor of $N$. **original_conjecture_false**: This is FALSE — Ahlswede and Khachatrian (1992) found counterexamples where the Ahlswede-Khachatrian optimal family construction exceeds both candidates. **counterexample_exists**: Witnesses a specific $N > 1$ where $\text{maxGCDIntersecting}(N) > \max(N/p, |\text{evenMultiplesSharing}(N)|)$. This failure motivated the search for the correct, more complex characterization.
mathContext:
OriginalConjecture ↔ ∀ N > 1, maxGCDIntersecting N = max (N / N.minFac) (evenMultiplesSharing N).card
original_conjecture_false : ¬OriginalConjecture
counterexample_exists : ∃ N > 1, maxGCDIntersecting N > max (N / N.minFac) (evenMultiplesSharing N).card

title: Ahlswede-Khachatrian Theorem (1996)
content:
**optimalFamily N j primes**: Integers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ divisible by at least one of $2q_1, \ldots, 2q_j$ or by the product $q_1 \cdot q_2 \cdots q_j$, where $q_1 < \cdots < q_j$ are prime factors of $N$. The $2q_i$ terms capture multiples of even numbers divisible by $q_i$; the product term captures multiples of the full product. The construction balances between using more $2q_i$ factors (larger $j$, more multiples per factor but larger product) and fewer (smaller $j$, fewer factors but smaller product with more multiples).

**ahlswede_khachatrian_theorem**: For every $N > 1$, there exists an optimal $j$ and a list of prime factors of $N$ such that $\text{maxGCDIntersecting}(N)$ equals the size of the corresponding optimal family. This completely characterizes the answer to Erdős Problem #534.
mathContext:
optimalFamily N j primes = (interval N).filter (fun n => (primes.take j).map (2*·)).any (·∣n) ∨ (primes.take j).foldl (·*·) 1 ∣ n)
ahlswede_khachatrian_theorem : ∀ N > 1, ∃ j primes, (∀ p ∈ primes, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ N) ∧ maxGCDIntersecting N = (optimalFamily N j primes).card

title: Special Cases
content:
**prime_power_case**: For $N = p^k$ (prime power), $\text{maxGCDIntersecting}(p^k) = p^{k-1}$. Since $N$ has only one prime factor $p$, every element of $A$ must be divisible by $p$. There are exactly $p^{k-1}$ multiples of $p$ in $\{1,\ldots,p^k\}$, and they form a GCD-intersecting set.

**two_times_prime_case**: For $N = 2p$ (odd prime $p$), $\text{maxGCDIntersecting}(2p) = 2$. Any element sharing a factor with $N = 2p$ must be even or divisible by $p$. But even numbers not divisible by $p$ are coprime to odd multiples of $p$, so the only valid set is $\{2p\}$ plus one partner that shares a factor with $2p$, giving size 2.
mathContext:
prime_power_case : ∀ p k, p.Prime → k ≥ 1 → maxGCDIntersecting (p^k) = p^(k-1)
two_times_prime_case : ∀ p, p.Prime → p > 2 → maxGCDIntersecting (2*p) = 2

title: Summary Theorem
content: **erdos_534_summary**: Packages the three central results into a single conjunction: (1) the Erdős-Graham conjecture is false (`original_conjecture_false`), (2) a concrete counterexample exists (`counterexample_exists`), and (3) the correct Ahlswede-Khachatrian characterization holds for all $N > 1$ (`ahlswede_khachatrian_theorem`). The proof is a direct construction from the three axioms via `⟨_, _, _⟩`.
mathContext:
erdos_534_summary : ¬OriginalConjecture ∧ (∃ N > 1, ...) ∧ (∀ N > 1, ∃ j primes, ...)
Proof: exact ⟨original_conjecture_false, counterexample_exists, ahlswede_khachatrian_theorem⟩
